title: Past Tense Endings
subtitle: -ED: /t/, /d/, and /ɪd/
description: The -ED ending is pronounced three different ways depending on the final sound of the verb. Getting this right makes your English sound smooth and natural.
tip: After voiceless sounds (k, p, s, f) say /t/; after voiced sounds (g, b, z, v) say /d/; after T or D, say /ɪd/ — it gets its own syllable.
phrases: Yesterday I walked to the park, jogged around the lake, and started a new book.
She cooked dinner, cleaned the kitchen, and decided to rest.
He jumped, skipped, and landed softly on the padded mat.
They talked, laughed, and ended the evening with a toast.
We visited the museum, watched a film, and rested at the hotel.
He worked all day, fixed the sink, and needed a long nap.
